title: Histamine-poly(maleic anhydride) conjugate improves selective cellular uptake of Fe 3 O 4  magnetic nanoparticles for dual-modal MRI/SPECT cancer imaging
content: Advanced magnetic nanoparticles (MNPs) are increasingly studied as multifunctional contrast agents for medical imaging applications. We aimed to introduce MNPs decorated with a poly(maleic anhydride-alt-1-octadecene)-histamine conjugate (PMAO-His) to serve as a targeted contrast system for dual-modality MR/SPECT imaging. FE-SEM analysis showed that Fe3O4@PMAO-His had an average diameter of 25–30 nm. The MNPs were pH-sensitive and could change their size and charge in response to pH variations. In the MTT assay, the prepared Fe3O4@PMAO-His exhibited no toxicity toward normal cells (MCF-10A) and demonstrated cytotoxicity in breast cancerous cell lines (MDA-MB-231 and MCF-7). MRI analysis (in vitro) indicated that the MNPs provided T2-weighted signal reduction as Fe concentrations were increased. Following incubation with MNPs, MDA-MB-231 cells exhibited a greater reduction in MRI signal intensity than MCF-10A cells. A simple and effective method was developed for chelator-free radiolabeling of Fe3O4@PMAO-His with 99mTc. The maximum labeling yield was obtained 97% using Fe3O4@PMAO-His at pH 7.5, following a 40 min reaction time at room temperature. It also exhibited high stability in human serum and saline. The biodistribution results on Balb/c mice showed predominant hepatobiliary uptake with minimal accumulation in the kidneys, heart, and lungs. The PMAO-His conjugate endowed Fe3O4 MNPs with improved water dispersibility, chelator-free radiolabeling ability, pH-sensitive surface charge switchable behavior, low toxicity, selective cellular uptake, and faster clearance, warranting further investigation.
